## Docket 1.2.5

**A page served instead of the page is not the page's content.**

Two false claims fixed, both about content Docket was never actually shown.

**Transcriptions are finished work.** An archive of WWI nursing diaries had six
transcripts reported at HIGH as "unfinished content is live and indexable". The
marker was `xxxxx`, and the context was the transcriber's convention for
handwriting they could not read. Runs that vary in length are standing in for
text; a field somebody forgot to fill in is one token typed once. A short page
and a single stray run still fire, so a genuine placeholder is still caught.

**A browser-upgrade notice is not thin content.** "20 pages have almost no
content" — fifteen of them were a notice saying the browser was out of date,
served with HTTP 200 in place of the page. Docket no longer judges the writing
of a page it was not given, and says so plainly instead of dropping those pages
in silence. It states what that establishes and what it does not: Docket does
not impersonate Googlebot to find out what search engines receive.
